subject: Aurora Retail workshop — hybrid vs onsite options & runbook
messages:
From: Claire Tan <claire.tan@aurora-retail.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — hands-on workshop options

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're keen to move into a hands-on POC workshop to validate routing/load behavior and run a short prompt review with our catalog team. A few questions to help us schedule:

- Do you support a hybrid setup (some onsite attendees + remote viewers)?
- We expect a throughput test with up to 20 concurrent designer users; can you support a load window?
- What are the visitor access requirements for your on-site engineers?

We'd like to target the week of Sep 20. Our prefered window is mornings (10:00–13:00 PT) so it overlaps EMEA late afternoon.

Can you share a short runbook and the draft agenda so I can check with Security for recording permissions?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Tan
VP Product, Aurora Retail
claire.tan@aurora-retail.com
+1 415 555 0193
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tan <claire.tan@aurora-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on workshop options

Hi Claire — great to hear Aurora wants to move forward. Short answers up front: hybrid is supported, we can run a controlled load window, and we can provide a runbook draft.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm attendee list and onsite headcount (we send an engineer for onsite support if >=2 onsite attendees).
2) Pick a date/time slot: Sep 21 or Sep 23, 10:00–13:00 PT (we can do 09:30–12:30 if you want prep time).
3) I'll attach a short runbook (draft) and a site access form we ask customers to complete for badges/visitor access.
4) Please confirm recording permissions (we ask for permission before enabling any recording).

On the load test: we usually run staged ramp-ups — 5, 10, then 20 concurrent simulated clients across a 30–45 minute window. Aditya will be the SE running the throughput harness; looping him in.

Attachments: runbook (draft) and site_access_form (fill and return).

If hybrid, we recommend an AV feed + screen-share (we can stream the terminal and the dashboard). Onsite room requirements: projector or large TV, wired network option for load tests (preferred), and a quiet room for engineers to sit with participants.

Available times above — tell me which date you prefer and who will be onsite.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tan <claire.tan@aurora-retail.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on workshop options

Thanks all — quick logistics notes from my side (CS/ops):

- Onsite visitor access: Aurora typically needs a completed site_access_form (attached) with full legal name, company, and ID type for each guest. Security often requires this 48 hours before arrival.
- AV: HDMI + audio out is sufficient; if you want us to record, we'll need written permission.
- Recording & privacy: we redacted any customer tokens in saved logs. If Aurora's security team needs SOC/SAML details, we can pull a short evidence pack.

I attached the site_access_form_Aurora.docx — Claire, if you can push that to Security, we'll take care of the rest.

On the load test note: Aditya and I will coordinate the harness and throttling so the production-like traffic doesn't touch live keys. We'll use a staging model pinned to the runbook's config.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks, Sergio / Marissa — good plan. Hybrid works best for us:

Onsite attendees (tentative):
- Claire Tan (VP Product)
- Raj Patel (Eng Manager)
- 2 members of our Catalog team (on-site)

Remote attendees: analytics and security ( ~8 people).

We prefer Sep 23, 09:30–12:30 PT.

A few clarifying items:
- Recording: security will want to review — can you provide the recording endpoint and retention policy in writing?
- Slides & screen share: will Redwood host the recording and distribute slides, or do you want Aurora to host?

Claire

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on workshop options

Claire — confirmed Sep 23, 09:30–12:30 PT. Thanks for the attendee list. A few specifics to close out:

1) Recording & retention: Redwood will host the recording in a secured bucket (private link). Retention: 30 days by default; we can arrange a shorter window on request. We'll deliver the recording link and a redacted transcript. If Aurora needs longer retention, we can set a custom policy (we'll add to the bill of materials).

2) Slides / share: Redwood can host the recording + slides on a private Drive folder and share links post-session. If Aurora prefers to publish internally we can deliver raw files only.

3) Load test: confirmed — all simulated clients run against staging models and staging endpoints; no production keys. We'll provide the traffic ramp plan in the runbook.

4) Onsite logistics: please return the completed site_access_form at least 48 hours before Sep 23. For guests we'll need: full name, company, phone, and ID type. Our on-site engineer (Aditya) will arrive 30–45 minutes prior to validate network.

5) AV & network: wired ethernet for the load generator is strongly preferred; if not possible we will throttle accordingly.

Attached: redwood_workshop_runbook_v1.pdf (draft) — includes agenda, traffic plan, roles, and checklist.

Please reply with explicit permission to record (we'll do one more confirmation at the start of session). Once you confirm, I'll send the calendar invite and the Drive link.

Best,
Sergio
